title: Build a tile board
prompt: Write arena() returning an integer array of shape (32,18), zero except 6 at y=20,x=4. Example: arena()[20,4] is 6.
solution:
import numpy as np
def arena():
    a=np.zeros((32,18),dtype=int)
    a[20,4]=6
    return a
tests:
a=arena()
assert a.shape==(32,18), 'Use 32 rows and 18 columns'
assert a.dtype.kind in 'iu', 'Use integer storage'
assert a[20,4]==6 and a.sum()==6, 'Only tile (4,20) should contain 6'

title: Regenerate elixir
prompt: Write regen(values,gain), returning a float array capped at 10 without changing values. Example: [9,2] plus 2 gives [10,4].
tests:
a=np.array([9.5,1.0])
assert np.allclose(regen(a,1),[10,2]), 'Add and cap each value'
assert np.allclose(a,[9.5,1]), 'Preserve input'
assert np.allclose(regen([0],.5),[.5]), 'Keep fractional regeneration'

title: Affordable costs
prompt: Write affordable(costs,elixir) returning costs <= elixir in original order. Example: [6,1,4] at 4 gives [1,4].
solution:
import numpy as np
def affordable(costs,elixir):
    a=np.asarray(costs)
    return a[a<=elixir]
tests:
assert np.array_equal(affordable([6,1,4],4),[1,4]), 'Include equal costs and preserve order'
assert affordable([6],0).size==0, 'Return an empty array if none are affordable'

title: Feature offsets
prompt: Write offset(rows,adjustment) to add one offset per column. Example: [[1,2]] plus [10,20] gives [[11,22]].
tests:
